The decided foundation:
- surface (light or dark): Dark
- display-type (the heading typeface): IBM Plex Sans. Shown with the reason: Built for developer tools and open-source like Argus. Titles read clean and neutral on a dark screen, keeping the root-cause explanation the focus.
- body-type (the body typeface): Source Sans 3. Shown with the reason: Made by Adobe for its own docs and given away free, like your MIT project. Its plain, slightly narrow letters match IBM Plex Sans, so small paragraphs look like the same family as your headings.

reply.summary: Your foundation is built for a dark screen, because Argus runs in terminals and dashboards where engineers already stare at dark UI all day. The softer IBM Plex Sans headings and Source Sans 3 body text keep long root-cause explanations easy to read, while the tight 4px spacing and 8px rounded corners let dense metric and container rows stay packed without feeling cramped. Subtle shadows keep panels layered but calm, so the plain-language root cause is the thing that stands out.
reply.rule: #28a4f0 is your brand colour, used on the GitHub and docs buttons, links and active nav, while #14b8a6 supports secondary actions like filters and #fbbf24 marks the AI investigator; greys carry all the plain structure and the status colours only ever appear on real metric states.

reasons.surface: Dark suits an open-source monitoring tool that people run on their own servers, and it keeps long log and metric views easy on the eyes.
reasons.display-type: IBM Plex Sans is made for developer tools and open-source, so your headings read clean and neutral on dark and leave the root-cause explanation as the focus.
reasons.body-type: Source Sans 3 comes from Adobe's own free docs and is given away under an open licence like your MIT project, and its plain letters sit well beside IBM Plex Sans.
reasons.type-scale: 15px body with headings at ×1.25 keeps root-cause write-ups and docs readable while still fitting many metric and container rows on screen.
reasons.brand-color: #28a4f0 gives the GitHub and docs links, the main buttons and active states one clear identity colour, so visitors always know where to click next.
reasons.secondary-color: #14b8a6 marks supporting actions like filters and toggles, so they read as related to the brand without competing with it.
reasons.accent-color: #fbbf24 draws the eye to the AI investigator, matching how Argus highlights the moment it finds a likely root cause.
reasons.neutral: Cool greys match the dark, technical feel of a server tool and give all the plain text, borders and panels a calm, even base.
reasons.semantics: #34d399, #f59e0b and #f87171 map to healthy, warning and failing metrics, so anyone scanning a dashboard reads status in a glance.
reasons.spacing: Tight 4px spacing packs in metric values and container rows, which suits monitoring screens where people compare many numbers at once.
reasons.radius: Soft 8px corners keep panels, cards and buttons feeling modern and friendly without looking playful.
reasons.depth: Subtle shadows separate panels and popovers from the dark background while keeping the interface flat and calm.
